newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania govt sets new foreign investment rules.
newsitem.headline: Romania govt sets new foreign investment rules.

text.p: Romania's government approved on Wednesday a decree on foreign investment, setting down long-awaited rules on portfolio flows seen as pivotal for capital market growth and attracting foreign funds.
The decree establishes for the first time clear rules on capital gains, setting tax on gains repatriation at four percent, sharply lower than a proposed 18 percent in an initial draft.
Capital gains will be repatriated only in the currency in which the initial investment was made. The invested capital is not submitted to taxation if repatriated, a government statement said.
Economic Reform Minister Ulm Spineanu said the decree would become effective once published in the Official Gazette.
"We want to develop capital markets but we have to keep in mind the hardship encountered by the Czech Republic...," Spineanu said, referring to recent turmoil caused by portfolio investors outflows.

If capital gains withdrawn sooner than a year exceed 25 percent of the total value of the investment, authorities will impose an extra tax of 0.1 percent per day of the amount repatriated calculated for the whole year.
"The 0.1 percent tax will regulate an excessive appetite for speculation," Spineanu said. Brokers said the supplementary tax was meant to limit portfolio investors' volatile movements.
Current laws cover only direct investment and no institution has so far been authorised to issue portfolio investor certificates to serve in repatriation-related foreign exchange operations.
